correctness.rationale: At 29, a fourth root of -5 exists (4), and 29 is unramified in the splitting field. The Frobenius conjugacy class fixes the fourth root and acts as 29 on ζ40; Chebotarev gives positive density. Every prime in this class is 29 mod40 with -5 a fourth power; its odd order yields q|H5(a), while q=-1 mod5 yields 5|Hq(2). Reciprocity calculation is exact. Modular seed and independent exact checker returned VERIFY_OK. No integral-n statement made.

value.rationale: The full reciprocal-gcd integrality problem is organized by local divisibility graphs. This theorem changes the qualitative picture for unrestricted prime-power interactions from finite witnesses to a positive-density infinite family with one exponent fixed, while correctly separating those interactions from the much stronger integral-n problem. The quadratic-reciprocity obstruction is an additional structural restriction, not a standalone novelty claim.
